ideas.name: NVIDIA Corporation
ideas.thesis: NVDA appeared in all 22 of 22 overnight screens with unanimous high conviction — the clearest consensus idea in today's digest. Reporting Q2 FY2027 earnings on August 26 after close, consensus expects ~96% YoY revenue growth ($93.63B, revised up 6.7% in 3 months) and EPS of $2.13 (~2x YoY), yet the stock trades at just 21.1x forward earnings — in line with the S&P 500 despite dramatically superior growth. The 34.6% gap between the current ~$225 price and the 68-analyst consensus target of $303.09 underscores a valuation dislocation. Options are strongly preferred: the market is pricing ~7% implied move vs. a 4-quarter average realized move of only ~2.8%, making a bull call spread (e.g., Aug 29 expiry) a more capital-efficient structure than outright stock ahead of this binary event.
ideas.catalyst: Q2 FY2027 earnings after market close on August 26, 2026 — 4 days away; July PCE print drops the same morning, compressing two major catalysts into one session
ideas.edge: 68-analyst consensus PT of $303.09 vs. ~$225 current = ~34.6% upside gap; options market pricing ~7% implied move vs. ~2.8% average realized move over last 4 quarters — defined-risk spread structures (e.g., bull call spread) are capital-efficient; 85% analyst buy consensus; EPS consensus $2.13 (~2x YoY)
ideas.bull_case: A beat-and-raise on revenue ($93.63B+ est.) and EPS ($2.13 est.) with continued HBM/data center demand confirmation could trigger a rapid re-rating toward the $303 consensus target; at 21x forward earnings, valuation provides cover for multiple expansion on upside surprise.
ideas.bear_case: Shares have declined after each of the last 4 earnings reports ('sell-the-news'), and elevated pre-earnings IV means option premium is expensive — a modest beat or cautious guidance could still result in a 5–10% drawdown; Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote 36 hours later adds a macro overlay risk.

ideas.name: SK Hynix Inc. Sponsored ADR
ideas.thesis: SKHY appeared in all 22 of 22 overnight screens with unanimous high conviction, making it the joint top consensus idea. As NVIDIA's primary HBM memory supplier and a locked-in partner in the $500B+ Nvidia/SK Group AI infrastructure deal, SKHY is the most direct equity read-through on an NVDA earnings beat. The stock has pulled back ~35% from July highs despite reporting record 76% operating margins and 257% YoY revenue growth in Q2 2026, creating a pronounced valuation dislocation. A KRW 40 trillion (~$29B) share buyback announced August 19 and Barclays' reiterated Buy on August 20 add further near-term catalysts.
ideas.catalyst: NVDA Q2 FY2027 earnings on August 26 as primary HBM demand read-through; KRW 40 trillion buyback announced August 19, 2026; Barclays Buy reiteration August 20, 2026
ideas.edge: Consensus analyst PT of $245.46 vs. ~$163 last close = ~50% upside gap; stock down ~35% from July peak despite record 76% operating margin and 257% YoY revenue growth — sentiment-driven dislocation vs. fundamentals; $500B+ Nvidia supply partnership with 10 long-term contracts provides revenue visibility; Temasek sovereign capital deployment reported
ideas.bull_case: A positive NVDA print confirming accelerating HBM demand is the clearest re-rating catalyst, and the buyback provides a structural price floor; Barclays and JPMorgan both bullish, with a 50% gap to consensus target offering substantial upside if ADR liquidity normalizes.
ideas.bear_case: NVDA earnings miss or cautious HBM4 ramp commentary could extend SKHY's drawdown further; ADR liquidity and Korean won FX risk add friction; the 35% July selloff suggests headline sentiment can overwhelm fundamentals in the short term.

ideas.name: Invesco QQQ Trust (Nasdaq-100 ETF)
ideas.thesis: QQQ appeared in 19 of 22 overnight screens, flagged as the cleanest liquid vehicle to express a directional or volatility view on the August 26–28 triple-catalyst cluster (NVDA earnings, July PCE, and Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote). The Nasdaq-100 snapped a 5-day losing streak on August 21 but tech is still down 3%+ over the prior week, setting up a mean-reversion setup if NVDA beats and Warsh is neutral; conversely, a hawkish Warsh surprise or NVDA miss could compress multiples violently given the 30-year yield at a 19-year high of 5.28%. Screens favored both directional call spreads (bull case) and protective put spreads (hedge case) — with straddles/strangles as a vol play for those not picking direction.
ideas.catalyst: NVDA earnings August 26 after close; July PCE + Q2 GDP second estimate August 26 pre-market; Fed Chair Warsh Jackson Hole keynote August 28 ~10am ET
ideas.edge: QQQ +16.8% YTD but tech sector -3%+ over the prior 5 days; 69% of fund managers expect a neutral Warsh tone — already priced in, making hawkish surprise the asymmetric risk; a 2022 analog saw S&P fall 3%+ on Jackson Hole day; defined-risk options (call spread or put spread) limit exposure to yield-shock tail risk; potential 2–4% single-session reprice if NVDA beats and Warsh is stable
ideas.bull_case: A strong NVDA print combined with a neutral-to-dovish Warsh tone could reprice QQQ 2–4% in a single session as the final major Mag-7 earnings report clears the calendar and long-end yield fears ease.
ideas.bear_case: A hawkish Warsh surprise — even modestly so — against a backdrop of 5.28% 30-year yields and a 3%+ recent tech drawdown could compress Nasdaq multiples sharply; an NVDA miss compounding macro noise would be doubly damaging.

ideas.name: Energy Select Sector SPDR Fund
ideas.thesis: XLE appeared in 7 of 22 overnight screens, consistently flagged as the cleanest liquid vehicle to express the ongoing Iran geopolitical risk premium. Trump's 'economic warfare' vow against Iran (August 19–20), UAE suspending trade with Tehran, and Brent crude at ~$93.61 sustain the energy inflation trade. With S&P energy earnings projected to grow 57% in CY2026 and refiner margins at multi-year highs, the fundamental backdrop supports the sector even before geopolitical premium. All runs recommended options over outright ETF to manage the binary ceasefire headline risk.
ideas.catalyst: Ongoing US-Iran escalation with Strait of Hormuz disruption risk; Trump 'economic warfare' rhetoric August 19–20; Jackson Hole (Aug 27–29) rate signal as a macro overlay that could amplify or cap the energy inflation trade
ideas.edge: XLE +32–44% YTD leading all S&P sectors; Brent at $93.61 still well below April 2026 peak of ~$120, leaving upside room if Hormuz tensions escalate; S&P energy sector earnings projected +57% in CY2026; refiner margins (VLO, MPC) at multi-year highs; geopolitical risk premiums historically persist 3–12 months once established
ideas.bull_case: Continued Iran escalation and Hormuz disruption risk keeps Brent elevated toward prior highs; 57% earnings growth and record refiner margins support sector fundamentals independent of geopolitics; defined-risk call spreads capture upside with limited downside.
ideas.bear_case: A diplomatic ceasefire headline is the primary tail risk and could unwind the geopolitical premium rapidly; Jackson Hole hawkishness that strengthens the dollar could cap commodity prices; XLE already up 32–44% YTD limits incremental buyers.

ideas.name: Apple Inc.
ideas.thesis: AAPL appeared in 4 of 22 overnight screens as a medium-conviction defensive tech idea. The stock pulled back ~0.9–2.9% from recent highs on August 21 despite reporting a record June quarter ($109.4B revenue +16% YoY, EPS $2.02 +29% YoY) and 9 consecutive EPS beats — a short-term dislocation screens flagged as a potential swing re-entry. With no near-term earnings catalyst until ~October 2026, AAPL's appeal is defensive resilience: lower beta than semis into the volatile August 26–28 macro window, a Services segment at record $30.74B, and an indirect AI narrative beneficiary via a newly announced $10B AI lab backed by NVDA and AAPL (August 21).
ideas.catalyst: No near-term earnings catalyst (next ~October 2026); indirect catalyst: $10B AI lab announcement August 21, 2026; macro clarity from Jackson Hole PCE print August 26–28 could benefit defensive tech broadly

ideas.bull_case: Record fundamentals, 9 consecutive EPS beats, and a growing AI narrative (new $10B lab) support a re-rating toward the $363 consensus target; defensive low-beta profile makes AAPL a relative safe haven if macro volatility spikes around Jackson Hole.
ideas.bear_case: No near-term earnings catalyst means the stock may drift without a specific trigger; rate-sensitive growth multiples remain a headwind at 30-year yields of 5.28%; the post-record-quarter dip could deepen if broader tech sells off on NVDA miss or hawkish Warsh.

ideas.name: SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust
ideas.thesis: SPY appeared in 4 of 22 overnight screens, exclusively as a hedging instrument rather than a directional long. With the S&P 500 down ~1.4% week-to-date through August 21, sovereign yields at multi-decade highs (30-year at 5.33%), and three binary catalysts landing August 26–28, short-dated put spreads on SPY offer cost-effective portfolio-level protection on existing tech and semi longs. The asymmetric risk is to the downside: 69% of fund managers already price in a neutral Warsh tone, meaning a hawkish surprise is the unpriced tail — the 2022 analog saw the S&P fall 3%+ on Jackson Hole day alone.
ideas.catalyst: Fed Chair Warsh debut Jackson Hole keynote August 28 ~10am ET (most binary event); July PCE + Q2 GDP second estimate August 26 pre-market; September FOMC September 15–16 with fresh dot plot; 30% market-implied probability of a September rate hike
ideas.edge: Neutral Warsh tone already 69% priced — hawkish surprise is the asymmetric unpriced risk; S&P fell 3%+ on Jackson Hole 2022; 30-year yield at 5.33% (19-year high) actively compresses equity multiples; US fiscal deficit $432B in July alone; short-dated put spreads are cost-efficient given recent vol pickup; 765 identified as key SPY support zone on hawkish shock
ideas.bull_case: A neutral-to-dovish Warsh tone combined with in-line PCE data could relieve long-end yield pressure and send SPY higher, making the hedge cost a cheap insurance premium that expires worthless in a benign scenario.
ideas.bear_case: A hawkish Warsh surprise — backed by 3 July FOMC dissents favoring a hike and a 30% market-implied Sep hike probability — could push SPY toward the 765 support zone in a single session, validating the put spread structure; Iran escalation and fiscal concerns add secondary pressure.
